titleEn: The Glory of Kings — God's Presence Everywhere (ch. 101)
about: God, speaking in the first person, orders a first, clean outer court for the Ark and declares that he is present everywhere: with Daniel, Jonah, Joseph and Jeremiah, beneath the stacked layers of creation, above the heavens, with the Son and the Holy Spirit.

sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፻፩ is the numeral 101 (፻ = 100, ፩ = 1). በእንተ is 'concerning' (the usual heading formula); ህላዌ is a verbal noun of ሀሎ 'to be, exist' ('being, existence'), and ኵለሄ is 'everywhere' (ኵሉ 'all' + the place-ending -ሄ); the wording is close to 'concerning existence-everywhere'. The title is ours, not a manuscript's.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይቤሎ ፡ ግበር ፡ ላቲ ፡ ዐጸደ ፡ ቀዳሚ ፡ ዴዴ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይባእ ፡ ህየ ፡ ሥኡብ ፡ ወርኩስ ፡ ወዘኢኮነ ፡ ንጹሐ ፡ እስመ ፡ አነ ፡ እሄሉ ፡ ኀቤሃ ፡ ወአኮ ፡ ህየ ፡ ባሕቲታ ፡ አላ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ አምሳሊሃ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ይጼዋዕ ፡ ስምየ ፡ በንጽሕ ፤
sentences.l: And-again he-said to-him: Make for-her a-court first, round-about(?), that not may-enter there the-defiled and-unclean and-who-not he-is clean, for I I-will-be with-her, and-not there alone-of-her but where all her-likenesses, where is-called my-name in-purity;
sentences.i: And again he said to him: Make for her a first court all around (?), so that no one defiled or unclean, nor anyone who is not clean, may enter there. For I will be with her, and not only there, but wherever any of her likenesses are, wherever my name is called upon in purity.
sentences.n: Start here: ወካዕበ is ወ- 'and' + ካዕበ 'again, a second time'; ይቤሎ is 'he said to him' (ይቤ 'he said' + -ሎ 'to him'), the standard way the text introduces a speaker, and what follows is God speaking in the first person; the addressee is not named in this part, and the speech seems to concern the dwelling being prepared for the Ark (ታቦት, feminine, hence ላቲ 'for her' and ኀቤሃ 'with her') (?). ግበር is the imperative 'make!'. ዴዴ is uncertain (?): I read it as 'all around, round about', but it may mean something else and I offer it only as a guess; ዐጸደ ቀዳሚ is 'a first (outer) court'. ከመ ኢይባእ 'so that ... not enter' is the purpose pattern: ከመ + a subjunctive verb, here negated by ኢ-. ሥኡብ and ወርኩስ are adjectives of uncleanness; ዘኢኮነ ንጹሐ is a ዘ- relative, 'he who is not clean' ('he who is not' ዘ-ኢ-ኮነ + 'clean'). እስመ 'for, because'; እሄሉ is the first-person subjunctive/imperfect of ሀሎ 'to be', 'I will be / I am to be'; ወአኮ 'and not'; ባሕቲታ 'alone' with the possessive -ታ 'her'; አምሳሊሃ 'her likenesses' (the copies of the Ark). ይጼዋዕ ስምየ is 'is called my name', i.e. 'my name is invoked'. The lexical calls here (ዴዴ above all) are hedged.

sentences.t: ሀሎኩ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ዳንኤል ፡ ውስተ ፡ ግብ ፡ ወሀሎኩ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ዮናስ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ከርሠ ፡ ዐንበሪ ፡ ወህሎኩ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ዮሴፍ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ግብ ፡ ወሀሎኩ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ኤርምያስ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዐዘቅተ ፡ ዐምዐም ፤
sentences.l: I-have-been with Daniel in the-pit, and-I-have-been with Jonah in the-belly-of the-great-fish, and-I-was with Joseph in the-pit, and-I-have-been with Jeremiah in the-well-of mire;
sentences.i: I was with Daniel in the pit, and I was with Jonah in the belly of the great fish, and I was with Joseph in the pit, and I was with Jeremiah in the well of mud.
sentences.n: Start here: ሀሎኩ is the perfect of ሀሎ 'to be, be present' in the first person singular, 'I was / I have been (present)'; it is the refrain of the passage and begins nearly every unit below. ምስለ 'with', ውስተ 'in, into'. Four scriptural rescues are named: Daniel in the lions' den (Daniel 6), Jonah in the belly of the great fish (Jonah 1:17; ዐንበሪ is a large sea creature, here 'great fish'), Joseph in the pit (Genesis 37), and Jeremiah in the muddy cistern (Jeremiah 38:6). ግብ is the 'pit' or 'den' (used for both Daniel and Joseph). ከርሠ ዐንበሪ is a construct chain, 'belly-of (the) great-fish'; likewise ዐዘቅተ ዐምዐም 'well-of mire' (I take ዐምዐም as 'mud, mire' (?)). The third ሀሎኩ is spelled ወህሎኩ here, with a different first letter; this looks like a spelling variant of the same verb, not a different word.

sentences.t: ሀሎኩ ፡ አዐምድ ፡ ታሕተ ፡ መትሕተ ፡ ታሕቲት ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይሰጠሙ ፡ አድባር ፡ መትሕተ ፡ ማያት ፡ ወሀሎኩ ፡ መትሕተ ፡ ማያት ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይሰጠሙ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ እሳት ፡ ወተይ ፡ ሀሎኩ ፡ አዐምድ ፡ መትሕተ ፡ እሳት ፡ ወተይ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይሰጠሙ ፡ መልዕልተ ፡ ነፋሳት ፡ ወዛሕል ፡ ሀሎኩ ፡ መትሕተ ፡ ነፋሳት ፡ ወዛሕል ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይሰጠሙ ፡ መትሕተ ፡ ጽልመት ፡ ወመትሕቴሃኒ ፡ ለጽልመት ፡ ወለቀላያት ፡ አነ ፡ አዐምድ ፡ ወኀቤየ ፡ ያሰምክ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ፍጥረት ፡ ወኪያየ ፡ ይጸወን ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ዘፈጠርኩ ፤
sentences.l: I-have-been I-support beneath the-below-of the-lowest, that not they-sink the-mountains beneath the-waters, and-I-have-been beneath the-waters, that not they-sink upon the-fire and ተይ; I-have-been I-support beneath the-fire and ተይ, that not they-sink above the-winds and ዛሕል; I-have-been beneath the-winds and ዛሕል, that not they-sink beneath the-darkness, and-beneath-it-too for-the-darkness, and-for-the-deeps I I-support, and-on-me leans all creation, and-me is-borne all that I-created;
sentences.i: I have been supporting them beneath the lowest of the low, so that the mountains do not sink beneath the waters; and I have been beneath the waters, so that they do not sink upon the fire and ተይ (?); I have been supporting beneath the fire and ተይ (?), so that they do not sink above the winds and ዛሕል (?); I have been beneath the winds and ዛሕል (?), so that they do not sink beneath the darkness, and beneath even the darkness, and I hold up the deeps. All creation leans on me, and by me everything that I created is borne.
sentences.n: Start here: this is one long chain of stacked supports, each layer held up by God from beneath: mountains over waters, waters over fire, fire over winds, winds over darkness and the deeps. There is no ፤ inside it to cut at, so it stays one unit. ሀሎኩ አዐምድ is 'I have been (and am) supporting': ሀሎኩ + a present-habitual verb; አዐምድ is 'I make stand / I prop up' (from ዐምድ 'pillar', so 'I act as a pillar') (?). መትሕተ and ታሕተ both mean 'beneath'; ታሕቲት is 'lowest' or 'lower part' ('beneath the below of the lowest'). ከመ ኢይሰጠሙ 'that they not sink' is ከመ + negative subjunctive, a purpose clause, with ይሰጠሙ 'they sink' (plural, subject the mountains/waters/etc.). ወተይ and ወዛሕል are crux words (?): I cannot identify ተይ or ዛሕል with confidence, and they may be names or terms for cosmic elements or levels; I leave them untranslated, and a printed or scribal corruption is possible. ወመትሕቴሃኒ 'and beneath it too' has the emphatic -ኒ ('also, even'). ቀላያት is 'the deeps, the seas'. ያሰምክ 'it leans / is made to rest on' (from the root 'to lean, rest on'; the causative is used with ኀቤየ 'on me') (?). ይጸወን 'is borne, carried' (?). ዘፈጠርኩ is a ዘ- relative, 'that which I created', with ፈጠርኩ 'I created' as the first-person perfect (-ኩ).

sentences.t: ህሎኩ ፡ መልዕልተ ፡ ምድር ፡ ወሀሎኩ ፡ አጽናፈ ፡ ዓለም ፡ እሰፍን ፡ ኵሎ ፤
sentences.l: I-have-been above the-earth, and-I-have-been the-ends-of the-world I-measure all;
sentences.i: I have been above the earth, and I have been at the ends of the world, measuring everything.
sentences.n: Start here: ህሎኩ is again a spelling variant of ሀሎኩ 'I have been'. አጽናፈ ዓለም 'ends-of the-world' is a construct chain; I take አጽናፈ here as 'at the ends', an accusative of place (?). እሰፍን is 'I measure / extend' (?), the root can mean to measure out or to stretch; I choose 'measure'. ኵሎ is the accusative 'everything'.

sentences.t: ሀሎኩ ፡ በአየር ፡ ማኅደርየ ፡ ወሀሎኩ ፡ መልዕልተ ፡ ሰረገላ ፡ ኪሩቤል ፡ እሴባሕ ፡ ወትረ ፡ እምኵሉ ፡ መላእክት ፡ ወሰ ፡ ብእ ፡ ቅዱሳን ፤
sentences.l: I-have-been in-the-air my-dwelling, and-I-have-been above the-chariot-of the-cherubim I-am-praised always by-all angels and ሰ ብእ holy;
sentences.i: I have been in the air, my dwelling place, and I have been above the chariot of the cherubim, praised always by all the angels and by holy men (?).
sentences.n: Start here: በአየር is በ- 'in' + አየር 'air'; ማኅደርየ is 'my dwelling' (ማኅደር + -የ 'my'). ሰረገላ ኪሩቤል 'chariot-of cherubim' is another construct chain, recalling Ezekiel's chariot vision (Ezekiel 1 and 10). እሴባሕ is 'I am praised' (a passive/reflexive stem, first person) (?), and ወትረ is 'always, continually'. The end is a crux (?): the text prints ወሰ ፡ ብእ with a space; I read it as ወሰብእ 'and men', so 'by all angels and holy men', but ወሰ ('and also') plus an odd ብእ is possible. ቅዱሳን 'holy ones' is the plural of ቅዱስ.

sentences.i: And I have been above the heights, filling everywhere.
sentences.n: Start here: አርያም is 'height, the highest heaven'. እመልእ 'I fill' (first person present) and ኵለሄ 'everywhere' again, the same word as in the chapter heading, so this is the chapter's theme.

sentences.t: ሀሎኩ ፡ መልዕልተ ፡ ፯ ፡ ሰማያት ፡ እሬኢ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ወእፈትን ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ዘይሴወር ፡ እምኔየ ፤
sentences.l: I-have-been above 7 heavens I-see all and-I-test all, and-there-is-not what is-hidden from-me;
sentences.i: I have been above the seven heavens, seeing all things and testing all things, and nothing is hidden from me.
sentences.n: Start here: ፯ is the numeral 7, a word in this system (read 'seven'); ሰማያት is 'heavens'. እሬኢ 'I see' and ወእፈትን 'and I test, try' are first-person present verbs; testing the minds and hearts is a biblical divine act (Psalm 7:9; Jeremiah 17:10). አልቦ 'there is not' (negative existential) with a ዘ- relative, ዘይሴወር 'who/that is hidden' (a passive/reflexive stem of 'hide') (?); እምኔየ 'from me' (እም- 'from' + -ኔየ).

sentences.t: አነ ፡ ህልው ፡ ውስተ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ መካን ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ባዕደ ፡ አምላከ ፡ ዘእንበሌየ ፡ በሰማይ ፡ በላዕሉ ፡ ወበምድር ፡ በታሕቱ ፤
sentences.l: I Existing in all place, and-there-is-not another god besides-me, in-heaven above and-on-earth below;
sentences.i: I exist in every place, and there is no other god besides me, in heaven above or on earth below.
sentences.n: Start here: ህልው is a participle/adjective 'existing, present', related to ሀሎ and to ህላዌ in the heading; with አነ 'I' it makes a verbless sentence, 'I am existing'. ዘእንበሌየ is 'besides me, without me' (ዘእንበለ + -የ). በላዕሉ and በታሕቱ are 'above (it)' and 'below (it)'; the -ሉ and -ቱ are 'its'. The words recall Deuteronomy 4:39 and the commandment 'no other gods before me' (Exodus 20:3); I note the echo, not a quotation.

sentences.l: There-is-not what resembles me, said the-Lord;
sentences.i: There is none who is like me, says the Lord.
sentences.n: Start here: ዘይመስል 'who resembles' (ዘ- relative + 'he resembles'); ኪያየ is the object form 'me' (ኪያ- + -የ), after 'resemble'. ይቤ እግዚኣብሔር is the quotation formula 'the Lord said'; it appears inside the speech, which marks that what precedes (and follows) is God's own utterance, so it reads as a reminder of the speaker. Compare Isaiah 46:9, 'there is none like me' (?: the echo is general).

sentences.t: እዴየ ፡ ሣረረታ ፡ ለምድር ፡ ወየማንየ ፡ አጽንዐታ ፡ ለሰማይ ፡ አነ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ወልድየ ፡ ወመንፈስ ፡ ቅዱስ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: My-hand founded-her the-earth, and-my-right-hand made-firm-her the-heaven; I with my-son and-spirit holy.
sentences.i: My hand founded the earth, and my right hand made firm the heavens; I am with my Son and the Holy Spirit.
sentences.n: Start here: ሣረረታ is 'he/it laid-the-foundation of her'; the object suffix -ታ 'her' is doubled by ለምድር 'the earth' (ለ- marks the object here), which is a regular Geʿez way of marking a known object; likewise አጽንዐታ ለሰማይ 'made-her-firm the heaven'. Compare Isaiah 48:13 'my hand laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand spread out the heavens'. እዴየ 'my hand' and የማንየ 'my right hand' (የማን 'right') are the subjects. The last clause, 'I with my Son and the Holy Spirit', is a Trinitarian statement; the -የ in ወልድየ is 'my'. The part ends with the row of ፨ marks, which close the section and are attached to this last unit.
